leading_positions.synthesis: Four members each prefer B028 alone as the whole prize, in each case citing a Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction paired with the Jarillo-Herrero experiments and the breadth of opening support. Three of the four (Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson) moved to it from a different opening first choice; Mehlig did likewise from B003. Three members name all three credited laureates, Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and Pearce and Danielsson list B028 only as an alternative. Shared: the superconducting mechanism is unsettled and the first-author experimental team and other moire groups are outside the credited names. Not shared: whether these points make the prize early or are merely interpretive, and whether Bistritzer belongs with MacDonald.

Four members include B022 in their preferred configuration with Katori and Ye as laureates; Kroll and Lindroth prefer it alone, while Danielsson and Pearce pair it with B002. Shared: a clean two-name attribution, independent reproduction at the 10^-18 level, and reach into tests of constants, geodesy and a redefinition of the second. Not shared: whether it stands alone or needs a partner, and how much weight to give its overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson list it only as an alternative, and Danielsson and Eriksson describe its fundamental-physics reach as prospective in part.

Two members prefer a two-part prize of IceCube (Halzen alone) and the optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye), describing the pair as two distinct achievements with no common theme. Both voice the same reservation: one name for a collaboration-scale discovery, with AMANDA-era figures outside the credit. Danielsson would exclude the Galactic-plane result from any citation as too recent. Kroll and Lindroth, who prefer B022 alone, explicitly doubt B002 for the same attribution reason, and Lindroth would not pair the two without a joint argument. No other member lists B002 in a preferred configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members ranked B028 and four placed it in their top three; no member disputes that the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states are reproduced and real.
B022 is judged clean on attribution (Katori and Ye) and mature by members who rank it first or highly, including those who do not prefer it.
The scientific rank of B037 is not disputed by anyone who addressed it; the objection raised is attribution (conception and construction of the detectors versus the 2012 analysis leadership).
Several members explicitly say the unsettled origin of the superconductivity should not by itself decide B028, and that any citation should be worded around flat bands and correlated phases.
scientific_disputes: Whether B022 is a distinct step beyond the comb-based (2005) and ion-clock (2012) work, as Lindroth and Pearce argue, or an incremental refinement and more technological than conceptual, as Mehlig argues and Kroll and Lindroth acknowledge as a counterargument.
Whether the fundamental-physics consequences of B022, such as constants and dark-matter bounds, are demonstrated or still prospective (Danielsson, Eriksson).

Whether IceCube's diffuse-flux detection, the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane result are equally secure; Kroll regards source identification as incomplete and Danielsson would keep the Galactic-plane result out of any citation.
Whether B028 is sufficiently understood as a discovery when the nature of the correlated insulators and pairing remains debated.
attribution_disputes: B002: whether Halzen alone, as conceiver and long-term leader, captures the decisive credit for a collaboration of hundreds, and how AMANDA-era contributors should be treated.

B037: whether Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as conceivers and builders of ATLAS and CMS can stand for the discovery, given that the 2012 analysis leadership is a different group and a principle for crediting detector architects has not been agreed.
B028: whether Bistritzer should share the theory credit with MacDonald, and how to treat Yuan Cao and the other first authors and the Dean and Young groups under a three-name limit.
B022: Katori's lattice concept versus Ye's accuracy and many-body clock work, with Lemonde and others uncredited.
B031 versus B048: Pearce and Olsson discuss Kane and Molenkamp without Mele, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang; Olsson would not extend the prize to Xue, and Eriksson prefers the narrower B048.
B014: the four-name credit list does not fit three places, and Johansson, Eriksson and Pearce see Girvin versus Blais as unresolved.
maturity_disputes: Whether B028, with experiments dating from 2018 and an unresolved pairing mechanism, is early (Danielsson, Kroll, Johansson, Olsson, Mehlig and Eriksson each acknowledge the risk) or secure as a platform discovery (Olsson, Eriksson, Johansson).
Whether the pending redefinition of the second bears on the timing of B022; Pearce and Lindroth say the case does not rest on it, while Kroll cites it as supporting timing.

Whether B001 carries a maturity standard comparable to that applied to B028, given its still-debated interface mechanism (Mehlig, Eriksson); Olsson ranked it first but did not make it her preferred configuration.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B014 and other superconducting-circuit candidates): research field is circuit QED, directs WACQT at Chalmers, has Chalmers colleagues and collaborators in the area, and moved away from B014 for that reason.

Kroll (B022): doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, in the community from which the Ye group's work grew; no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye; the committee may judge whether recusal is needed.

Pearce (chair, B002): astroparticle physics at KTH with PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur ties, none documented with IceCube or Halzen; B002 is in his own field. B033 is close to his gamma-ray work but is not in his configuration.
Lindroth (B022): atomic structure is close to her field; she flags closeness, with no conflict with Katori or Ye.
Eriksson (B018, B028, B048): intellectual proximity through electronic-structure theory; no documented relationship with credited people.
Mehlig (B003): intellectual adjacency through neural-network and statistical-physics work; no documented tie to the credited names.

Olsson (B001): works on LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interfaces by electron microscopy and flags caution in advocating it; also notes a Chalmers connection with Johansson, with no shared project on shortlisted candidates.
questions_for_round2: Is the committee prepared to award the whole prize to B028 alone, or should it be paired, and if so with which candidate?
Should B022 be awarded alone or in a two-part prize, and if paired, is B002 or another partner such as B037 or B028 more defensible?
For B002, can the committee state a principle under which Halzen alone is the decisive credit for IceCube, and what do external experts say about the AMANDA-to-IceCube history?
Can the committee agree a principle for crediting detector architects in B037, and if not, is B037 off the table this year?
Does the unsettled superconducting mechanism in B028 make the prize premature, or can a citation limited to flat bands and correlated phases be defended on reproducible measurements?

For B028, should the laureates be MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero or all three of Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and can Cao's and the Dean group's contributions be addressed in the citation?
Is B022 distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes that its citation can name the lattice clock explicitly without reading as a second clock prize?
Does Kroll's Boulder connection or any other disclosed flag require a recusal or only a note in the record?
summary.chair_observation: Preferred configurations split into two groups of four on single-theme or paired outcomes: four members prefer B028 alone and four include B022, two of whom also include B002. B028 and B022 draw the strongest explicit cross-support, and each is also listed as an alternative by members who prefer the other. Disagreement is mostly about attribution and timing rather than the quality of the underlying science. The B002 and B037 questions turn on how the committee credits collaboration-scale discoveries, which is a matter to settle in round 2. The chair's own configuration includes B002, which is in his field, and that is disclosed above.
